findings.location: p. 4, Sec. Exercise training versus usual care, line 71
findings.evidence: 'analysis were primarily RCTs (83%; n=15/21) ( Underlying data, File 6) ^': 15/21 = 71.4%, but the text reports 83%.

'SMD 0.70 [95% CI 0.15, 1.24]; p=0.31) ( Figure 3) compared with usua': The 95% CI [0.15, 1.24] excludes the null value 0, but the reported p is = 0.31; significance at alpha = 0.05 disagrees. p implied by the CI (Altman-Bland) is about 0.012.

'-0.67 [95% CI -1.31, 0.03]; p=0.04) ( Figure 8), and rise from sup': The 95% CI [-1.31, 0.03] includes the null value 0, but the reported p is = 0.04; significance at alpha = 0.05 disagrees. p implied by the CI (Altman-Bland) is about 0.05.

'SMD -0.06 [95% CI -0.23, -0.11]; p=0.46) ( Table 2; Extended data, Figu': The 95% CI [-0.23, -0.11] excludes the null value 0, but the reported p is = 0.46; significance at alpha = 0.05 disagrees. p implied by the CI (Altman-Bland) is about 0.05.
'SMD -0.06 [95% CI -0.23, -0.11]; p=0.46) ( Table 2; Extended data, Figu': Estimate -0.06 lies outside its own 95% CI [-0.23, -0.11].

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'An individual-participant-data re-analysis of 312 patients from eight of these trials confirmed the VO _2peak benefit (SMD 0.61 [95% CI 0.33, 0.89]).'. Its head count 312 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 're-analysis' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.

The paper names Egger's test ("…tion bias was assessed via funnel plots with trim and fill, and estimated using Egger’s regression intercept ^[16]. The quality of evidence for outcomes was rated us…"), but no matching call (/regtest|egger/) was found outside comments in 5 code file(s). Same pattern at 1 more place(s): Methods (statistical analysis) vs bp_work/code.

findings.location: Table 2 rows 'Isometric elbow flexion (HHD)' and 'Isometric knee extension' vs data/Pre.Post.csv column 'Side'
findings.evidence: data/Pre.Post.csv records 9 left-side and 9 right-side rows (Side=R/L) for elbow and knee strength; the paper does not say whether both sides of the same patient enter the same meta-analysis. Pooling both sides treats 18 rows as independent when they come from fewer patients. Our port: elbow SMD 0.32 [-0.24, 0.88] with both sides vs 0.07 [-0.27, 0.40] right side only (paper 0.07 [-0.26, 0.41]).

findings.location: Table 2 rows 'STS (seconds)' and 'Citrate synthase' (I2) vs our re-run
findings.evidence: Paper I2: STS seconds 58.5% (Abstract) / 58.05 (Table 2), citrate synthase 70.9%; our port of the same data gives 53.4% and 57.5%. The pooled SMDs also differ (STS -0.50 vs -0.65; citrate synthase 1.81 vs 1.45). The released data therefore do not reproduce these two rows; the paper does not state which rows or time points were used.
